reason: The verse says desire for women (பெண்ணாசை) leaves no way to desire heaven; desire is the shared topic, but there is no claim about wanting and liking diverging.
The verse claims a substance in the body, heated (காய்ச்சியபின்), gives strength (வீரியமாய்); it makes no claim about reversing ageing, so the ageing-hallmarks finding is only topical.
The verse wants to stop roaming for food for the belly (கும்பிக்கு இரைதேடி); it makes no claim about fasting or metabolism.
The twelve-legged horse (பன்னிரண்டு கால்புரவி) is the breath only by cipher; the verse names no nose or inhalation and claims nothing about memory or fear.
Untied dogs are no use as guards (கட்டாத நாய்), a figure for the senses; nothing about breath or lifespan.

The poet says he could not know the nature of ida and pingala (இடைபிங்கலையினியல்பு); the nasal cycle is about left-right alternation, which the verse does not state, and reading the channels as nostrils is a gloss.
The two lights (இருசுடர்) rising and setting in the sushumna are the two breaths only by cipher; the verse claims nothing about hemispheres or autonomic tone.
A confession of maya ending in the image of the painted wall (சுவராய்த் தோன்றும்); nothing about circadian clocks.
Knowing the One within (என்னிலே இருந்தஒன்றை); nothing about metal preparations.
The verse portrays alchemists (வாதம்செய்வேன்) as confidence tricksters; the finding on heavy metals in products sold online shares only the alchemy-and-metals topic.
The verse lists the signs of age: teeth falling, eyes darkening, grey hair and wrinkles (நரைதிரை), a staff; it describes ageing but claims nothing about its mechanism or reversibility.
The verse places the guru's seat at the uvula and sushumna (சுழுமுனை) and lists nose among the eight; no claim about nostril alternation.
The verse names meditation as silence (தியானமான மோனமே) at the crown; a theory of advanced meditation shares the topic, but the stanza is too obscure to carry a claim.

reason: A funeral scene of women weeping with unbound hair (தலைவிரித்து ... அழுதார்); death is the shared topic, but the verse makes no claim about how death reminders change attitudes.

The verse claims that eating an atom of the substance makes all the body's diseases fly away (வியாதி யெல்லாம் ... பறந்து போகும்) and gives body-siddhi; the finding concerns different, herbal Siddha decoctions in COVID trials, so linking them needs a generous reading.
The verse binds the horse by kundalini's vaasi (குண்டலி வாசியினால்) at the root; breath practice is the shared topic, but no claim about temperature or immunity, and the riding is cipher.
Shining like fire latent in bamboo (வேயில் கனல்) despite a low birth; no mantra or breathing.

The verse asks for a state without speech, breath, forgetting or remembering (மறப்பும் நினைப்பும்அற்று), dead while alive; the theory that advanced meditation leads to cessation of experience bears on such a state, but it is speculative and does not point either way.
Sun and moon (தவனசோமர்) at the gate are the two channels only by gloss, and the stanza is an incomplete sentence; no claim about nasal alternation.

reason: The verse longs for the 'I' to die (நான் இறந்து போக) before the body does; death is the shared topic only.
The verse watches the mother's hand burn to ash (வெந்துபொடிசாம்பலாகுதே); a death scene, but no claim about death reminders and worldview defence.
The verse vouches for an earlier alchemical book's salts and melts (சரக்கு, உருக்கினங்கள்) but makes no claim of turning mercury to gold; alchemy is the shared topic only.

The verse says that after tasting the great honey (பெருந்தேன்) the poet desires nothing else; adaptation of happiness is a related theme but the finding does not test a claim of lasting satiety in the Lord.
The verse redirects desire (இச்சித்திருக்கின்ற) from a woman's breast to the goddess; craving is shared, but no claim about wanting versus liking.

The verse says desire for sex does not die (ஆசை யழியா) while its pleasure is small (சிற்றின்பம்) beside release; reading this as wanting outlasting liking is generous, since the contrast is with spiritual bliss.
The verse asks to be already dead (மாண்டிருப்பது) before the body falls; death is the shared topic only.
The verse voices the ordinary belief that we shall not die (இறவாதிருப்பம்) and answers with the body lost; death denial is a related theme, but no claim about death reminders.
Union with the awareness that fills everything (எங்கெங்குமானதிலே); Bell tests are not evidence for a pervading awareness.
The silent Siva-yogi (மோனச் சிவயோகி) who does not speak in anger; meditation is the shared topic, but no claim about predictive models.
The medicine against dying (இறவாதிருக்க மருந்து) is named as remembering the Lord's feet, not a compound; artemisinin is irrelevant.
The verse asks whether japa and tapas (செபம், தவம்) were done only to lose the body, and what yoga alone yields; meditation's benefits are the shared topic, but no specific claim.
The body is writing on water (அப்பிலெழுத்து) and everything perishes; cell renewal shares only the body's impermanence.

The verse says thought runs about (ஓடித் திரியும் கருத்து) and must be caught and lodged in nada's end; the finding that minds wander and that people are less happy then shares the topic, but the verse claims nothing about happiness.
It must not be said (சொல்ல லாகாதே); solitude seen. No claim about predictive models.
Consciousness (சைதன்னியம்) above the three cosmic selves; nothing about gravity-related collapse experiments.
The verse says the mantras are within, the five letters of the mind (மனத்தின்ஐந்து எழுத்து); silent mantra is the shared topic but no claim about cortical activity.
An oil and perfume compound for a rite; it names no metals, so the heavy-metal finding does not apply.
The verse puns that the true rasavada (ரசவாதம்) is the root at home; alchemy is shared, but no claim about making gold.

The verse states a life of a hundred years is 21,600 breaths a day (இருபத்தோராயிரத்தோடறுநூறு சுவாசம்), that days shorten as breaths go out, and that if they do not go out there is no going (போகாவிட்டால் போவதில்லை); the finding that the fixed-stock idea rests only on a cross-species correlation and that slowing breath has not been shown to extend life tells against that hypothesis.

The verse claims the honey-kalpa (கற்பம்) ends hunger and anger and lets one watch Death's dance (கூற்றுவனார் ஆட்டம்); whether that means defeating death is unclear and the honey is cipher, so the lifespan-limit finding links only by topic.
